findings.text: Top level GICv2m initializer chooses firmware discovery path from parent handle kind, delegating to device tree walk when the handle denotes an OF node and to MADT parsing otherwise.

MSI allocation searches registered frames for a run of free SPIs satisfying count and natural alignment derived from count, reserves it atomically under a global spin lock, fails with no space when no frame fits, and on later setup failure releases the reservation and any parent mappings.

A single global spin lock serializes inspection and mutation of the frame list and per frame allocation bitmaps during reserve and release, held only around the bitmap search and update and not across IOMMU or parent domain operations.

A frame SPI window is accepted only when its base is at or above the architectural minimum, its count is nonzero, and the window end does not exceed the architectural maximum; violations are logged and rejected.

Device tree bringup enumerates child frames matching the v2m compatible, skips entries lacking controller marking, resolves resources, honors optional base and count overrides, initializes each frame, then creates the MSI parent domain; any failure unwinds all frames and reports an error.

Per frame setup maps the frame registers, prefers explicit SPI base and count when provided and otherwise derives them from the type register except on Graviton address only designs where explicit values are mandatory, validates the window, and records vendor specific SPI offset adjustments identified from the implementation identifier.

GICv2m advertises required MSI behaviours for default domain and chip operations with parent masking for PCI MSI, and supported behaviours covering generic flags plus MSI-X and multi MSI, with end of interrupt handling requested at the chip level.

ACPI bringup parses generic MSI frame subtables, rejects malformed entries, builds a memory resource for the frame, honors firmware SPI overrides, allocates a domain token, and initializes the frame, freeing the token when initialization fails.

When the MADT OEM identifier matches the Amazon value, the frame uses an enlarged mapping window, is marked address only, and multi PCI MSI support is withdrawn from the advertised parent capabilities.

ACPI initializer is idempotent once a positive frame count is recorded, otherwise parses all MADT MSI frames, creates domains, registers a provider returning the first frame token for PCI MSI, and on failure tears down all state and reports invalid argument; an alternate build always reports invalid argument.
Collection record pairs a 64 bit redistributor target address with a 16 bit collection identifier, used as the rendezvous between devices, events and CPUs.
Table descriptor holds a host base pointer, a 64 bit hardware value, an allocation order and a page size field, describing one ITS backing table.

ITS node aggregates command queue state, table array, collection array, firmware handle, MSI base callback, hardware type word, saved control state, affinity identifier, device list, flag word, list index, NUMA placement, domain flags and platform fixup fields, guarded by a raw spin lock for command paths and a mutex for device allocation.

Event to interrupt mapping keeps a bitmap of allocated LPIs, per event CPU collection indices, a hardware base, counts of physical and virtual mappings, a raw spin lock for virtual paths, and back pointers to virtual machine and virtual mapping arrays.

Device record links into its owning ITS list, references the parent node, embeds the event mapping, points at the interrupt translation table with size and entry count, and carries a numeric device identifier plus a sharing marker.

Command descriptor is a discriminated union of sixteen payload shapes covering invalidate, clear, trigger, map device, map collection, map translation, move, discard, invalidate all, virtual invalidate all, virtual map and move variants, doorbell invalidate and virtual SGI control, each carrying only the handles and identifiers its operation needs.

Queue entry is a four word raw command visible in host and little endian views; the queue occupies 64 KiB and its entry count is that size divided by the entry size, with builder callbacks resolving a collection or virtual processing element for a node.

ITS flag word reserves low bits for command queue flushing, two Cavium workarounds, forced non shareable memory and a Hisilicon workaround; redistributor local state uses bits for LPI enable, preallocated pending table and completed memory reservation.

LPI capacity derives from a global identifier bit count; property table size aligns the identifier space to 64 KiB and pending table size aligns one eighth of that space to 64 KiB, with a global default priority and 256 byte translation table alignment.

Maximum virtual processing element count is one shifted by a bit count that defaults to sixteen and grows when reduced VPE identifier support and virtual identifier length are advertised; virtualization level predicates test type word bits and device identifier width adds one to the encoded field.

Translation of an interrupt to its CPU takes the virtual element raw spin lock with interrupt state saved when a virtual element is involved and releases it symmetrically, while purely physical LPIs rely on the already held descriptor lock and perform no additional locking.

Event number is the hardware interrupt minus the device LPI base; collection lookup indexes per event CPU data, virtual mapping lookup is bounds checked and returns null when out of range, and the forwarding aware helper returns a virtual mapping only for interrupts marked forwarded to a virtual CPU.

Page allocation adds a global quirk to the caller GFP flags and requests decrypted memory, large translation tables allocate whole pages directly while small ones suballocate from a shared pool refilled one page at a time, and freeing mirrors that split with pool returns versus page release.

If transitioning a fresh allocation to decrypted or a freed range back to encrypted fails, the pages are intentionally leaked rather than freed because their attribute state is unknown, with the lower layer expected to have warned.

A collection is usable only when its low sixteen address bits are zero, otherwise validation warns once and yields null; a virtual element is usable only when its indexed collection passes that check.

Global proxy state combines a raw spin lock, a device pointer, an array of virtual element pointers and a victim cursor; per CPU accounting keeps separate atomic counters for managed and unmanaged LPIs.

Shareable memory support is the negation of a forced non shareable redistributor flag; the virtual move list is the bitmask of virtualization capable nodes that either support reduced identifiers or have virtual interrupts for the given virtual machine.

Out of range virtual mapping indices, misaligned collection addresses and requests for a firmware token when no ACPI frames are recorded trigger one shot warnings and fail safe null or error returns rather than proceeding with corrupt state.
Redistributor accessors resolve the current or selected CPU private region and derive control and virtual LPI bases with a fixed 128 KiB offset for the latter.
In scope helpers expose allocation of a real firmware node token from a physical address and a predicate reporting whether an interrupt is forwarded to a virtual CPU.

Teardown walks the frame list safely against removal, detaches each entry, releases its bitmap and mapping, drops firmware references including conditionally freeing irqchip tokens, and frees the frame record.

MSI domain operations delegate selection to the MSI library and bind allocation and release to the v2m implementations, while the parent descriptor fixes bus matching to PCI and platform MSI under a nexus token with a fixed name prefix.
Driver globals retain the redistributor aggregate, the parent interrupt domain, a bitmap of live ITS instances and a sequence number for virtual move operations.
